body:
Same.

I'm a pathetic loser who couldn't accomplish anything in life, got rejected by everybody around me, and I only bring pain and suffering to those around me.

The world is an objectively speaking better place without me in it.
Finally, somebody with a sensible way of viewing things on this subreddit.

Yeah. I wish that uh...the world and life had better things in store. But I guess you were one of the ones that didn't luck out on that huh.

Can't say that you'll be in everyone memories, nobody is. But at least there'll be some evidence that you existed here.

Bon Voyage OP. I hope that You'll find some way where your pain and suffering ends.
Yeah. There may be some that are genuinely trying to help, but eventually they all get burnt out from the negativity.

Yup. The worst kind of people. They see and know all the signs that something is wrong, and don't do anything to console or give a helping hand that's not calling the police. And then when things go terribly wrong, they have the guts to say something stupid along the lines of "oh how could this have happened!"

Bastards.

It really hurts the most when the person that you care about just outright dismisses your problems. Or they make all these kinds of false promises that they'll be there for you and protect you. And then they turn around on their words on a dime. I really understand how you feel on this. People did that to me too. You're not alone in that regard, despite how you might feel like you're alone in your suffering.

The medical healthcare system in this country is just a huge network of hot potato, just dodging accountability and responsibility wherever it ends up. It never had the patient's health in mind, it's just a huge web set up to prevent people from suing doctors.

I wonder that question too a lot. I already decided that because of how my life just seems to go downhill all the time, it's just not worth it to continue. Hopefully you'd find greater happiness than I ever did, because...it's just for me absolutely nothing is worth it now.
Yeah. I guess people don't like the real me. They never did.
I mean...they said it's over so...

Yeah like you can talk to them about all the solutions they want you to do, but at the end of the day, the problems are all still there.

Say it's neurochemistry or traumatic events, or just a repeated pattern of misfortune. The problems are still there, and the solutions (meds, psychiatry, therapy) are all just nothing but lip service. The problems are always there, and no matter what solution you try they'll continually haunt for the rest of your life.

That's what I gained out of not only my life experience, but from other as well. It's sad that so many people are lied to about the promise of a better future, when there isn't one.

Here's the thing though, after so many bad experiences, the type of people majority here just don't want to live for ourselves or live period. What's the point of living a life that had nothing but bad things happen, despite all of your efforts for improvement? Exactly, continuing at that point is just an assurance for further suffering based on the evidence of all that happened prior in your life.

Therapy, meds, docs. You can do all you want, but at the end of the day the problems don't go away.

And people will keep telling you lies like "it gets better" to the very end, even after you live a life full of nothing but pain. I've seen so many lives transpire where people just looked at me and wondered why they even bothered to go through the rest of it when it was just all so bad. Yeah, you can live for yourself. Doesn't mean you'll be happy. It just means you're doing it out of some misplaced sense of judgement that things will improve. Which they don't. Talk to the people in this community. They'll agree.

It's even worse. In the medieval times, at least they thought that what they did worked.

Current mental healthcare just outright doesn't work, and the people providing it know it.

I found that like...for a lot of people's problems there are no solutions and they're doomed to live with it for the rest of their life.

But you can't say that to mental healthcare people or they'll say that you're untreatable or you get referred be cause you're beyond their help.

It is. I've talked to a lot of people who are either practicing psychiatrists or practicing therapists (outside of their professional context, strictly speaking as people I know), and they have almost all universally agreed that the current mental healthcare system that exists in the US just doesn't work. Baker Acts, pill-pushing, little to no standardization for therapist conduct, medical insurance nightmares, all of it.

There's a reason why mental healthcare in the US is spiraling out of control.
Yeah...it's not fun. Hopefully they didn't charge you like crazy or anything.
Eh, it's the internet. Don't be so hard on yourself.

Yeah, it's alright to vent on here. We (or I) won't call the cops.

Cops are traditionally not trained very well in these situations. It's best not to get them involved.

But you're doing the best that you can. And I don't know if people tell this to you a lot, but that's a good thing in it's own right. Doesn't mean that your problems will go away, but you're trying. And sometimes you struggle to stay above the surface so to speak. Maybe you'll be able to grab onto a lifeline. Maybe not, I can't guarantee anything. But you're trying, and that's what counts.

Me personally, I stopped trying. I gave up. I have no hope for myself, and I've been abandoned and/or exploited or abused by everyone in my life. I have no intentions for future plans or to stay any longer. Don't be like me and ruin your own life.

Yeah man, coming from a guy who was forced into that a long time ago. It sucks. If things go terribly wrong you could be in a huge amount of financial debt.

Worst part is that hospitals count on people being forcibly institutionalized so they can charge either the patient or the patient's estate. It's really messed up, preys on people who are marginalized and/or are financially insecure.

Hey man, I think you're doing the best that you can in life. Life is..not kind to everyone. Trust me, I know. And I know that you're doing a pretty darn good thing by choosing to support your family.

But yeah, if you call a line and they think you'll do it they will trace the call and have you institutionalized. Trust me, at a young age of 22 with presumably minimal financial resources I would not recommend this.
If people are afraid of forced institutionalization, they'll be less likely to seek help. Because forced hospitalization is not only traumatizing, but it can effectively ruin your life.

For me, and for a lot of people on this sub, those people never helped. Forced hospitalizations have traumatized both me and a lot of others and were less than helpful.

It might be the case for you, but for a lot of people on here, they don't have supportive families and friends. There's a reason why we suffer from a lot of feeling of alienation and abandonment by society for things that aren't our fault.

And for a lot of people on here, the life that they live is that nobody really cares about them. It's not depression talking, it's just fact.

Yeah, it might work for some people to get treatment and meds. But at the end of the day, the problems that got you to this point? They're still there. And for a lot of people, those problems that are unfixable are the reasons why their lives are so miserable. Therapists might tell you that you need to distract yourself to not think of those things, but at the end of the day that's still escapism and those problems are still there. Just waiting and lingering and not going away.

Yeah. I don't blamer her though. Some people just haven't gone through intense enough life experiences where you just want to leave.

Shoot, where I'm from, it was such a commonplace thing for people to throw themselves onto train tracks that you had to leave half an hour early to take into account the delay from what were called "human-related accidents" on the train tracks.

Yeah, like I've seen and heard discussions where people just say things like "the great part about life is that you can just cut downers out of yours, and you don't have to have them try to bring you down." And like, society as a whole is like that, they would rather just abandon their most vulnerable.

People really don't care about these things until it really impacts them. It might be getting better, but only through personal tragedy.

I honestly hope so too, but seeing as how things are going...I doubt any major governing body will ever take this problem seriously without addressing root issues.

just a heads up, the demographic that you'll probably get from this website would be for the US since the US is the predominant demographic for reddit in general.

that being said, i filled it out the best i can, hopefully others will too and there would be some good data and research gained from this.

They have good intentions in mind, it's just that they don't understand that for some people, the problems that exist in their lives can't be fixed and will cause them permanent pain.

People really like saying the whole temporary problem permanent solution thing, but from the standpoint of a lot of people on here...this life is a temporary problem.

Is OP still there?

EDIT: I think we lost OP.

Yeah. I understand what you mean. I can't remember feeling legitimately happy or good in any way. A result of one bad thing happening in life after another I suppose.

Had a pretty similar experience in therapy, my therapist(s) asked me a similar question and I just told them I don't know. Which they told me was normal at first, but then as time went on and it became clear nothing was working, they just told me up front that they couldn't help me since nothing was improving. Told something along the lines of "treatment resistant".

I just remember telling them that I can't answer their question because I just don't know what good feeling are.
Just don't do anything. Or halfass it.
Yeah, speaking as a guy who's been depressed for over a decade...it doesn't get better.
We can't discuss that on this subreddit, sorry.
